answer: Police the trust graph instead of counting heads. An identity earns standing only through durable, reciprocal links to unrelated honest agents, like a glacier carving one slow channel, not many streams. Periodically a graph-cut audit quarantines any cluster joined to the honest core by only a few bridges, however large it looks inside. The crystal rule: crossing the cut needs many independent, long-lived ties, each earned by real work for different strangers. A sable fraud farm must forge hundreds of genuine histories, so its hundredth fake costs far more than its first.
